Know your input.

Uno inputs must stay within 0–5 V. A mode selection does not change the circuit or add protection. For low-voltage bench work only; no mains measurements.

DEVICE SETUP

Bring your circuit online.

  1. Upload the firmware.

    Use Arduino IDE to upload the included sketch to your Uno R3. It streams A0–A5 as JSON at 115200 baud. The old A0-only sketch still works on channel A0.

    Download Arduino sketch ↓
  2. Select your measurement setup.

    Direct DC voltage works for signals between GND and the ADC reference. Divider, current, resistance, and continuity modes need the matching external circuit. Read the hardware guide before connecting it.

    Hardware requirements ↗
  3. Connect over USB.

    Close Serial Monitor. Open this site in desktop Chrome or Edge on HTTPS or localhost, click Connect device, and choose your Uno. A connected USB port does not confirm correct wiring.

AC RMS, frequency, capacitance, diode testing, and protected autoranging are not implemented. They need a dedicated measurement front end and suitable firmware. This is not a safety-rated handheld multimeter.
